scenes.text: You're camping, and your tent door is just two flaps of fabric.
Wind blows them wide open. Bugs pour in.
So you put a rock on it. The wind flips it off.
So you tie it shut with string. Ten knots. Every single time.
So you sew on buttons. But bugs crawl right through the gaps.
So you get smart. Two rows of tiny teeth. Each one has a bump on top, and a hole underneath.
Then a slider squeezes them together, so every bump snaps into the next hole. One pull. Sealed.
Pull it back down, and a wedge pops them apart.
Wind. Bugs. Nothing gets in. You just invented the zipper.
An early version in eighteen ninety-three kept popping open. It took twenty years to fix. And you're probably wearing one right now.
